text: No, evidence does not confirm that a fire caused the 2021 tree-cover loss on the asset. The 81.3 hectares of tree-cover loss detected by Hansen/UMD in 2021 was within a planted forest (Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda) and the change was stand-replacing, but the Earth-observation data does not establish the cause. The loss could have been due to harvest, thinning, or other disturbances—fire is one possible explanation but not the only or confirmed one. The evidence only supports that tree cover was removed, not how or why.
